entries.title: II Corinthians 6:1
segments: Therefore, as God's fellow-workers, we also appeal to you not to receive his loving-kindness in vain.

entries.title: II Corinthians 6:2
segments: For he says--'At the time for acceptance I listened to thee, And on the day of deliverance I helped thee.' Now is the time for acceptance! Now is the day of deliverance!

entries.title: II Corinthians 6:3
segments: Never do we put an obstacle in any one's way, that no fault may be found with our ministry.

entries.title: II Corinthians 6:4
segments: No, we are trying to commend ourselves under all circumstances, as God's ministers should--in many an hour of endurance, in troubles, in hardships, in difficulties,

entries.title: II Corinthians 6:5
segments: In floggings, in imprisonments, in riots, in toils, in sleepless nights, in fastings;

entries.title: II Corinthians 6:6
segments: By purity, by knowledge, by patience, by kindliness, by holiness of spirit, by unfeigned love;

entries.title: II Corinthians 6:7
segments: By the Message of Truth, and by the power of God; by the weapons of righteousness in the right hand and in the left;

entries.title: II Corinthians 6:8
segments: Amid honor and disrepute, amid slander and praise; regarded as deceivers, yet proved to be true;

entries.title: II Corinthians 6:9
segments: As unknown, yet well-known; as at death's door, yet, see, we are living; as chastised, yet not killed;

entries.title: II Corinthians 6:10
segments: As saddened, yet always rejoicing; as poor, yet enriching many; as having nothing, and yet possessing all things!

entries.title: II Corinthians 6:11
segments: We have been speaking freely to you, men of Corinth; we have opened our heart;

entries.title: II Corinthians 6:12
segments: There is room there for you, yet there is not room, in your love, for us.

entries.title: II Corinthians 6:13
segments: Can you not in return--I appeal to you as I should to children--open your hearts to us?

entries.title: II Corinthians 6:14
segments: Do not enter into inconsistent relations with those who reject the Faith. For what partnership can there be between righteousness and lawlessness? or what has light to do with darkness?

entries.title: II Corinthians 6:15
segments: What harmony can there be between Christ and Belial? or what can those who accept the Faith have in common with those who reject it?

entries.title: II Corinthians 6:16
segments: What agreement can thee be between a temple of God and idols? And we are a temple of the Living God. That is what God meant when he said--'I will dwell among them, and walk among them; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.

entries.title: II Corinthians 6:17
segments: Therefore "Come out from among the nations, and separate yourselves from them," says the Lord, "and touch nothing impure; And I will welcome you;

entries.title: II Corinthians 6:18
segments: And I will be a father to you, and you shall be my sons and daughters," says the Lord, the Ruler of all.'
